newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway margarine no rival to Raisio -Mills.
newsitem.headline: Norway margarine no rival to Raisio -Mills.

text.p: Norwegian food producer Mills AS said on Wednesday a new cholesterol-cutting margarine it had launched did not pose a direct challenge to Finnish Raision Tehtaat's patented cholesterol-cutting product, Benecol.

"We say our product cuts the cholesterol level in the blood, but it is a completely different product from Benecol," Liv Kongsten, consumer information spokeswoman at Mills, said of the product called Vita.
"Vita does not have the patented component that Benecol has. Our product is made of rapeseed oil and sunflower oil," she told Reuters.
She said Oslo-based Mills, Norway's biggest manufacturer of margarine, launched Vita a few weeks ago on the Norwegian market.
"We don't see ourselves as a challenger of Benecol because we are only selling our product in Norway," Kongsten said.

Raisio, which so far sells Benecol only in Finland but plans to launch it in Sweden this year, cites research showing Benecol -- whose key ingredient is stanol esters -- cuts blood cholesterol levels by 10 to 14 percent.

Raisio's stock in Helsinki has recently come under pressure amid various market rumours, including talk of a new Norwegian challenger for Benecol. But in late Wednesday trade it was up 9.00 markka at 393.00.
Kongsten said Mills did not put a figure on how much Vita reduces the cholesterol level. "It is all relative to what you eat."
Mills, which also produces juice, mayonnaise and other foodstuff, has 360 employees and an annual turnover 1.5 billion crowns. The company is not listed.
